messages.subject: Ordering of factors in (aesthetics/legends)
parts:
Dear list,
I have come across a bug in ggplot2. Any help you can provide will be
helpful.

The bug involves inconsistent assigning of aesthestics to factor/
character data. I am trying to produce many individual plots from
multiple data sets. As in the example below, my factor/character data
is constant over the data sets (see ctry), but may be randomly
ordered. When producing multiple plots, the aesthetics seem to "train"
themselves in the order that the data is encountered. This is
different than how as.factor would treat the data. as.factor first
sorts the data and then assigns levels.

<CODE>

require(ggplot2)

# Code to illustrate mis-ordering of factors on different plots.
# Seems to set "aes" based on order, not level of as.factor(data)

ctry <- rep(c("US","UK", "EU", "JP"), each = 5)
x <- (runif(20) - 1 * 5)
y <- (runif(20) - 1 * 5)

plotData <- data.frame(ctry, x, y, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
sapply(plotData, class)


p1 <- qplot(x, y, data = plotData, geom="point", colour = ctry)
p2 <- qplot(x, y, data = plotData[order(plotData$ctry), ],
geom="point", colour = ctry)

plotData.f <- plotData
plotData.f[, "ctry"] <- as.factor(plotData.f[, "ctry"])
sapply(plotData.f, class)

p1.f <- qplot(x, y, data = plotData.f, geom="point", colour = ctry)
p2.f <- qplot(x, y, data = plotData.f[order(plotData.f$ctry), ],
geom="point", colour = ctry)

# How as.factor treats the data
# note that kk assigns level 1 to "BR", as does ll ---> consistent
treatment
# regardless of data order
kk <- as.factor(plotData[, "ctry"])
ll <- as.factor(plotData[order(plotData$ctry), "ctry"])

# > sessionInfo()
# R version 2.8.1 (2008-12-22)
# i386-apple-darwin8.11.1
#
# locale:
# en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/C/C/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8
#
# attached base packages:
# [1] grid stats graphics grDevices utils datasets
# [7] methods base
#
# other attached packages:
# [1] ggplot2_0.8.2 reshape_0.8.2 plyr_0.1.4 proto_0.3-8

messages.subject: Re: Ordering of factors in (aesthetics/legends)
parts:
Hi Brandon,

Yes, this is a bug, and it's fixed in the development version.

Hadley
